incident-bot: [ALERT] p95 latency spike on runtime-prod detected 2100001234. Route: text-gen/v2. Error rate up, some 502s. Pager routed to #eng-releases and #eng-oncall @here
Priya: I'm oncall — looking at dashboards now. p95 up ~420ms > threshold, spike started ~21:05 UTC
Arun: that was during the canary rollout. We pushed kernel-scheduler v2 + batching heuristics at ~21:04
Maya: I'm nearby, can help with pod restarts if needed. Handoff in ~10 if Priya needs to handoff
Julian: got an FYI from CS, looks like a customer (Acme AI) seeing timeouts. tagging CS for updates
Lena: CS: Acme reported ~20% failed requests and long tails since 21:06. They've escalated to priority. Sending them an acknowledgement now
Priya: looking at worker logs — seeing repeated "kernel_fallback=true" lines and many single-item batches. KV cache hits look fine.
Arun: hmm that's consistent. New scheduler path seems to pick a fallback kernel for certain padding patterns. Locally I can reproduce with the same model and padding multiples of 8
Priya: which feature flag controls the new selector? Can we flip it?
Arun: flag is runtime.canary.kernel_v2_selector. Flipping it should route canary nodes back to legacy kernel selection. Command: ```redwood-cli flags set runtime.canary.kernel_v2_selector false --env=prod```
Priya: executing the flag flip now
deploy-bot: [ACTION] runtime.canary.kernel_v2_selector set to false by Priya at 2100001290. Rolling change to canary pools
incident-bot: [INFO] After flag flip: initial telemetry shows p95 dropping within ~30s on canary shards
Maya: still seeing a handful of 502s from shard-3; those pods have cached the v2 kernel artifacts. I'll cycle those pods
Priya: shard-3 restart done — observing improved success rates on that shard
Arun: recommend rollback of the entire canary rollout (r-2026-04-kernv2). The change introduced a batching selection edge-case; need a patch before any further rollout
Priya: initiating rollback of release r-2026-04-kernv2 now
deploy-bot: [ACTION] rollback started by Priya at 2100001360 for r-2026-04-kernv2. Rolling traffic back to stable kernel path
incident-bot: [METRIC] error rate: 4.2% -> 0.6% within 2m after rollback start. p95 returned close to baseline
Julian: Lena, confirmed recovery for Acme?
Lena: Acme says latency normalized ~3 minutes after rollback. CS sent an update and will follow up with a post-incident note. No active escalations now
Maya: I'll hand on-call to Arun for postmortem work and overnight watch. Priya, are you comfortable with handing off?
Priya: handing off to Arun. All critical alerts cleared, pager status ok. I'll stay reachable if needed
Arun: taking over. I'll collect logs, reproduce, and open a blameless postmortem. Initial hypothesis: batching selection bug in kernel-scheduler v2 interacting badly with quantized kernel path causing kernel fallback and single-item batches
Priya: tagging incident: canary, kernel-fallback, rollback, customer-impact
Arun: creating ticket INC-210000-1 and will attach deploy logs, flag toggle timeline, perf diffs, and a repro snippet. Assigning to eng-runtime + SRE
Arun: repro sketch (local):
```
# repro pseudo
for seq in sequences:
  padded = pad_to_multiple(seq, 8)
  selected = scheduler.select_kernel(padded, quantized=True)
  if selected == "fallback":
    log("kernel_fallback=true", seq_len=len(seq), padded_len=len(padded))
```
Priya: thanks. Maya, Julian — please add any customer comms artifacts to the ticket. Lena will coordinate ACME follow-up
Lena: CS will send a 1:1 update and request a short postmortem summary. Will loop back if they ask for deeper details
Maya: big thanks everyone :thumbsup: Good mitigation cadence. Please avoid promoting this kernel change until the fix lands and we validate on a staging canary
Priya: closing pager for now. If anything regresses I'll reopen
deploy-bot: [CLOSE] Incident closed by Priya at 2100001555
